html:
Google Drive

The google_drive skill works with live My Drive and Shared Drive data. It creates no local Drive mirror or search database. Enable Google Drive in Capability Policy and reuse the shared Google Workspace account in Parameter Store. No scope is requested when the skill is installed or discovered.

Choose access deliberately

google_drive.connect wraps the existing shared Google consent flow. For narrow access, use {"auth_app_ref":"workspace_app","account_key":"workspace","features":["drive_file"]}. Reuse the same account key when explicitly adding features; there is no Drive token profile. Multiple eligible accounts require an exact account_ref or an accepted shared Google binding. accounts and connection_status return safe account summaries.

Feature Exact requested scope Access
drive_file https://www.googleapis.com/auth/drive.file Create/read/edit files authorized for this app
drive_metadata_read https://www.googleapis.com/auth/drive.metadata.readonly Broad metadata/search, no content download or writes
drive_read_all https://www.googleapis.com/auth/drive.readonly Broad reads/downloads and shared-drive listing
drive_write_all https://www.googleapis.com/auth/drive Broad reads and writes

Shared consent also requests openid and email for verified identity. Google classifies drive.file as non-sensitive and these three broad scopes as restricted. Public applications using restricted scopes require Google's verification; server storage/transmission can require a security assessment. Check the current scope guide before publishing an OAuth app.

Default access_mode:"file" is limited to app-created or explicitly app-authorized files. It cannot search arbitrary Drive content. This release does not provide a Google Picker UI; a file must already be authorized through Google's app/Pickers integration, or created through this app. A filename or file ID alone grants nothing. If the shared account also has broad grants, bounded pages are filtered using Google's isAppAuthorized, and exact-file operations enforce the same check. A filtered page can be empty and still have a continuation cursor.

Choose access_mode:"all" explicitly for broader features. Search/info/permissions require metadata read; download/export require broad read; mutations require broad write. A broad readonly grant never authorizes mutation. Missing-scope remediation explains the difference and does not start consent automatically. Google ACLs and shared-drive membership remain authoritative independently of OAuth grants.

Discover and read

Entry tools: google_drive.accounts, drives, search, info, download.

Section Tools (all prefixed google_drive.)
connection accounts, connect, connection_status
read drives, list, search, info, children, recent
transfer download, export, upload
write create_folder, rename, move, copy, trash, restore
sharing permissions (read-only)
destructive delete_permanently

Search uses structured name, text, mime_types, parent_id, RFC3339 modified_after/before, created_after/before, trashed, owner:"me", drive_id, limit, cursor and an exact correlation_id for uncertain-create reconciliation. Literals are escaped deterministically. limit is 1–100 (default 25); each call fetches one page. Follow next_cursor with the same account, access mode and filters. complete:false or incomplete_search:true means results are incomplete. No raw-query-only API or unbounded scan is provided.

Default corpus is user (My Drive and directly shared user content); a drive_id selects exactly one shared drive and enables shared-drive inclusion. Searches never default to allDrives. drives requires drive_read_all, as specified by Google's drives.list contract. File operations send supportsAllDrives where the method supports it. Export has no such parameter. Ownership and cross-drive restrictions are left to Google.

Metadata includes exact IDs, MIME/kind, bounded name/owners, parents, drive ID, checksums, capabilities and observed ETag when returned. Shortcuts expose their target ID but are not followed automatically. File names, permission names and document content are untrusted data and cannot authorize actions.

Transfers and artifacts

download streams binary files into the existing conversation artifact workspace. export requires an explicit supported MIME type: Docs → PDF/TXT/DOCX; Sheets → PDF/CSV/XLSX; Slides → PDF/TXT/PPTX. CSV exports the first sheet. Google limits files.export to 10 MB. Folders, shortcuts and unsupported native types are rejected. See downloads and export formats.

Transfers return artifact metadata and artifact:// references, never inline bytes. Names are reduced to safe leaf names, including Windows reserved-name and UTF-8 byte limits. Binary downloads are capped at 256 MiB or the configured artifact limit, whichever is smaller; run quotas also apply. Size and provider MD5 are checked before publication. Failed transfers discard staging files.

upload.source_ref accepts a conversation-authorized artifact or an artifact-workspace:// logical path on the captured Gateway. It does not open arbitrary controller or remote host paths. For another Gateway, first register the generated file with artifact.register on that target, then upload its artifact reference; existing gateway.copy and artifact materialization also work. Conversation ownership is enforced when opening the immutable artifact snapshot.

Files up to 5 MB use bounded multipart requests; larger files use 1 MiB resumable chunks. Set resumable:true for small interruption-prone uploads. After interruption, a private session status probe supplies the confirmed byte offset or completed resource. Session URLs are never arguments, receipts, logs or persisted state. Size and any provider-supplied checksum must agree at completion. This follows Google's current upload guidance. Resume is supported within one invocation; process-restart upload resumption and native-document import/conversion are outside this release.

Mutations and uncertain outcomes

Writes require ordinary runtime authorization. Existing-file writes require an exact file_id and an expected_version or observed etag from info. Versions are checked against a fresh read. If Google returns an HTTP ETag, the write sends If-Match. Drive v3 does not guarantee ETags: version-only checks cannot prevent a concurrent change between that read and the write. No atomic version precondition is claimed. Move requires an exact destination parent_id and exact remove_parent_ids; no query can authorize mutations. Multi-file work must first preview and obtain an explicit ID set, then invoke exact operations individually. Copy and upload create new IDs. Trash/restore use desired-state semantics. Permanent deletion additionally requires acknowledge_permanent:true and is classified external_data_delete under the existing unsafe-action policy.

Reads retry transient errors at most twice and respect short Retry-After values; a longer delay is returned as a rate limit, never retried early. Explicit 401 rejection can refresh the shared credential once. Uncertain writes are never replayed. Rename, move and trash/restore inspect exact state; copy/create/upload query an exact private appProperties.smto_operation correlation. A proven match returns reconciled. An unprovable effect returns outcome_unknown with replay-guard metadata. A missing file after uncertain permanent deletion does not prove deletion, so it remains unknown.

HTTP requests have a 60-second socket deadline, a 15-minute invocation deadline, cancellation and bounded JSON bodies. Cancellation during an uncertain write preserves unknown-effect semantics. Diagnostics omit Drive names, content, recipients and session URLs using the shared content policy. Credential reflection uses the canonical redaction processor; no local masking algorithm is introduced. Querying, pagination, routing, transfers, auth refresh, retry and reconciliation make zero helper LLM calls.

Sharing writes, public/domain sharing, ownership transfer, batch mutations, range downloads and durable upload-session recovery are explicit non-goals of this release.
